Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.1: Listening and Speaking 8.1.2 Speaking Fluency sounds
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 8.1.2 Speaking Fluency sounds, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it necessary to tell a story accurately, expressively and at the right speed? 2. How can we enhance our articulation of sounds?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 8.1.2 Speaking Fluency sounds together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn- sharing knowledge: The learners acquire the skill by sharing information on the features that make an oral

narrative presentation effective.

Values:
Responsibility: The learner offers leadership and guidance as they perform an oral narrative accurately, expressively and at the

right speed and record themselves.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills: social awareness: The learner displays their strengths in narrating ant then performing an oral narrative and

articulation of sounds.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print texts

● Braille texts

● Electronic reading materials

● Digital devices with assistive technology

● Audio visual clips

Suggested Skills:

● Recognising the various realisations of sound /i:/ in an oral context.

● Describing a speaker’s accuracy, expressiveness and speed in an oral presentation.
